body.html:
Three gates, and then the mobile epic is done

The rendering work is finished and merged — the app draws all 70 registered PortableDoc block types, and CI now reds if that regresses. Nothing below is about rendering. What is left is three things only a person with credentials and hardware can do. This is the whole list: if it is not here, it does not need you.

Start here

3
Gates left
1
Blocking v1 ship
~1
Hands-on time, all three
2-4
Plus unattended download

Do them in this order. Gate 1 is both the cheapest and the only one blocking ship sign-off. Gate 3 is mostly an unattended OS download, so start its download early and do Gate 1 while it runs. Gate 2 has a hard ceiling — its client half needs a paid Apple Developer membership, because a free Personal Team cannot sign the push entitlement. If you do not hold one, do its server half and park the rest deliberately.

  1. 1. Gate 1 — second member seat
  2. 2. Gate 2 — push credentials
  3. 3. Gate 3 — device boot
  4. 4. Already done for you
  5. 5. Optional extras
#GateHands-onBlocksHard prerequisite
1Second member seat~30 minv1 ship sign-offA second real email account you control
2Push credentials~30 minv1.1 push onlyApple: PAID membership for the client half
3Device boot~30 min + downloadRoot criteria 2, 5, 7macOS Tahoe + Xcode 26.4; iPhone for Part B

Gate 1 — second real member seat

Why it cannot be faked. The Cloud team has exactly one seat (frikk, owner, undemotable). This gate exists to prove the app-token exchange mints for a non-admin seat — so a DB-inserted or fabricated user proves nothing. There is a recorded incident where a fabricated user went stale and started returning 404. Use a real second account.

  1. Find the team id — do not guess it

    Read it from the Cloud console or from the CLI. Never hardcode it.

    bp cloud teams ls
  2. Invite the second account, as the owner

    The response carries an accept_url — you need it in step 3.

  3. Accept in a browser signed in as the SECOND account

    Open the accept_url while signed in as the invitee, not as the owner. This is the step that most often goes wrong silently — an owner-session accept produces a seat that looks right and tests nothing.

  4. Verify the role actually landed as member

    The new row must read role=member — not admin. If it reads admin, the RBAC leg is untested and the gate is not discharged.

  5. Log in as that member
    bp login # complete the device-link flow as the SECOND account
  6. Re-run the smoke on the member's token

    Expect 13 ok. Keep the transcript — it is the evidence.

    tooling/mobile-smoke/smoke.sh

The two calls, exactly:

POST/v1/teams/:team_id/invitations
NameInTypeRequired
team_idpathuuidYes
emailbodystringYes
GET/v1/teams/:team_id/members
NameInTypeRequired
team_idpathuuidYes
The failure that matters
If the smoke passes as the owner but fails as the member, that is precisely the bug this gate was built to catch. Stop and report it — do not retry with an admin token, which would turn a real finding into a green tick.

Gate 2 — APNs and FCM credentials

The relay is built right up to the credential wall. Six values go into /opt/barkpark-cloud/.env on the control plane. The two platforms are independent — Android alone is a valid, useful state, so do not block on Apple if you only have Google.

If you are waiting on Apple verification
Do the Google half FIRST — it needs no Apple involvement at all. The platforms are independent and Android alone is a valid state, so while an Apple enrolment sits in verification you can complete FCM end to end: enable FCM API V1, take the service-account JSON, land it in the .env, restart, and register the relay. That satisfies criterion 1 (credential_status true for at least one platform) AND criterion 2 (the workspace-scoped webhook row) — this gate reaches 2 of 3 with zero Apple. Nothing is redone when APNs arrives; the two platforms sit side by side in the same .env.
You need your OWN Apple team. Being a member of other orgs does not give you one.

There is no "create an organization" button in the portal. Teams are not created — they are the RESULT of enrolling. Invitations add your Apple ID to other people's teams; they never produce a team of your own. Your existing Apple ID can hold your own membership alongside every membership you already have.

Choose Individual / Sole Proprietor, not Organization. Both cost $99/year and both grant the identical technical capability — App IDs, APNs keys, the push entitlement. Organization only adds a company name and member roles, and it demands a D-U-N-S number (days to obtain), a public functional website on your own domain, a legal entity, and authority to bind it. Individual needs none of that.

RequirementIndividual / Sole ProprietorOrganization
D-U-N-S numberNoRequired
Public website on own domainNoRequired
Legal entity + binding authorityNoRequired
Two-factor on the Apple AccountRequiredRequired
Legal name, no nicknamesRequiredRequired
Physical address (P.O. box rejected)RequiredRequired
Annual cost$99$99

Enrol at developer.apple.com/programs/enroll on the web, or through the Apple Developer app on an iPhone or iPad — the app route is usually smoother because it verifies your identity using the device. Fee waivers exist for nonprofits, accredited schools and government entities.

The trap once you have several teams: APNs keys and App IDs belong to ONE specific team. The App ID for cloud.barkpark.mobile and the APNs key must live in the SAME team — yours. A key from one team paired with an App ID from another fails authentication in a way that looks like a bad device token, which sends you hunting the wrong bug. Check the team selector on the account page before creating either one.

If you would rather not pay: should you hold Account Holder or Admin role in an org you are already a member of, you could create the App ID and key there instead — but that ties this app's identity to someone else's organization. Not recommended for your own product.

Where each value comes from: the APNs key, key id and team id from Apple's Keys page (create a key with the Apple Push Notifications service enabled — token-based APNs docs); the bundle id must already exist with the Push capability on Apple's Identifiers page; the FCM service-account JSON from Firebase → Service accounts, with FCM API V1 enabled.

Env varWhat it isThe trap that makes it silently useless
APNS_KEY_P8Full .p8 PEM contentsA single-line value with literal \n works — runtime.exs expands it
APNS_KEY_ID10-character key id—
APNS_TEAM_ID10-character team id—
APNS_BUNDLE_IDcloud.barkpark.mobileMUST equal ios.bundleIdentifier in apps/mobile/app.json, and that App ID must have Push registered
APNS_ENVsandbox or productionWrong value = every send 400s with BadDeviceToken
FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSONThe whole service-account file, verbatimFCM API V1 must be enabled on the project
  1. Write the six values and restart
    sudo vi /opt/barkpark-cloud/.env # add the six values# then restart the control plane
  2. Probe the credential status

    It must report true for at least one platform before you go further.

    # in a remote console:BarkparkCloud.Push.credential_status()
  3. Register the relay once — it is idempotent, team-admin
  4. Verify the webhook row is WORKSPACE-SCOPED

    The created chat_blocked row must have a non-nil workspace_id. A flat-path row gets nil and can never fire — it looks installed and is inert.

POST/v1/barkparks/b2b81e69-c79c-4eff-b6d7-84507d15b925/push-relay
NameInTypeRequired
idpathuuid (guerrilla)Yes
The ceiling, stated plainly
Not in this packet by construction: the client half — expo-notifications, the aps-environment entitlement, google-services.json. That needs the entitlements wave and a paid Apple membership. This is why Gate 3 can never retire Gate 2. Without a paid membership, do the server half above and record "client half parked — no paid Apple membership" as the blocker. That is a clean outcome, not a failure.

Gate 3 — device boot

Honest sizing: not minutes. The OS upgrade comes first — roughly 2 to 4 hours, almost all unattended download. Expo Go cannot work here, because MMKV v4 and react-native-nitro-modules are custom native modules; a dev build is mandatory.

Part A — toolchain only. No Apple account needed, and it discharges every layout clause on the Simulator.

  1. Install macOS Tahoe 26.5.2

    About 9.4 GiB, one restart. Do not stop at Sequoia 15.7.7 — it reaches only Xcode 26.0–26.3, below Expo SDK 56's floor of 26.4.

    softwareupdate --list-full-installers # then install Tahoe 26.5.2
  2. Install Xcode 26.4 or newer

    Xcode on the App Store (~10–17 GiB). Launch it once so it installs components, then point Command Line Tools at Xcode — today they are CLT 16.4.

    sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developerxcodebuild -version
  3. Install CocoaPods via Homebrew — not gem

    System Ruby is 2.6.10, below CocoaPods' 2.7.4 floor. Homebrew ships its own Ruby.

    brew install cocoapods
  4. Prebuild the iOS project

    No ios/ directory is committed — this project is managed / CNG prebuild.

    pnpm installcd apps/mobilenpx expo prebuild -p ios
  5. Boot it on the Simulator

    Needs no Apple ID. This covers the Class-B reflow sites, token geometry, the recycleItems decision, the archived shelf, the picker sheet, and blocks-in-chat with Mermaid islands.

    npx expo run:ios

Part B — physical iPhone, on a free Personal Team. Only if you actually have one. No iPhone has ever been paired to this Mac, so this is a question, not an assumption.

  1. Prepare the device

    Enable Developer Mode (the device restarts), then trust this Mac over USB.

  2. Sign with a free Apple ID

    Xcode → Settings → Accounts → add your Apple ID → automatic signing. The bundle id cloud.barkpark.mobile works as-is.

  3. Run on hardware
    npx expo run:ios --device
  4. Capture everything in ONE sitting

    Free Personal Team profiles expire after 7 days. Record: haptics feel across the registry including the needsYou warning; transcript scroll and fps plus follow mode; swipe-to-archive; and cascade auto-select with MRU across a relaunch.

    Before any MRU evidence counts, assert that MMKV is the live backing store and not the silent in-memory fallback — otherwise the MRU proof is vacuous.

If there is no iPhone — what to do instead

Record "no iPhone exists" as an explicit ruling on the task. The Simulator dispositions from Part A then become the discharge surface — the task's own criterion allows exactly this — and I will re-scope the affected root criteria. Push stays out either way: a free Personal Team cannot sign the push entitlement.

Already done for you

Two things that used to sit in Gate 3 are already discharged, so do not spend time on them. Tonight's crown slice built an 83.8 MB release APK and drove the Android emulator end to end: it paged 80 screens of a paper containing every block type, found zero unknown blocks, and kept six screenshots as artifacts. Three gates, and then the mobile epic is done

The rendering work is finished and merged — the app draws all 70 registered PortableDoc block types, and CI now reds if that regresses. Nothing below is about rendering. What is left is three things only a person with credentials and hardware can do. This is the whole list: if it is not here, it does not need you.

Start here

3
Gates left
1/3
Blocking v1 ship
~1/hour
Hands-on time, all three
2-4/hours
Plus unattended download

Do them in this order. Gate 1 is both the cheapest and the only one blocking ship sign-off. Gate 3 is mostly an unattended OS download, so start its download early and do Gate 1 while it runs. Gate 2 has a hard ceiling — its client half needs a paid Apple Developer membership, because a free Personal Team cannot sign the push entitlement. If you do not hold one, do its server half and park the rest deliberately.

  1. 1. Gate 1 — second member seat
  2. 2. Gate 2 — push credentials
  3. 3. Gate 3 — device boot
  4. 4. Already done for you
  5. 5. Optional extras
#GateHands-onBlocksHard prerequisite
1Second member seat~30 minv1 ship sign-offA second real email account you control
2Push credentials~30 minv1.1 push onlyApple: PAID membership for the client half
3Device boot~30 min + downloadRoot criteria 2, 5, 7macOS Tahoe + Xcode 26.4; iPhone for Part B

Gate 1 — second real member seat

Why it cannot be faked. The Cloud team has exactly one seat (frikk, owner, undemotable). This gate exists to prove the app-token exchange mints for a non-admin seat — so a DB-inserted or fabricated user proves nothing. There is a recorded incident where a fabricated user went stale and started returning 404. Use a real second account.

  1. Find the team id — do not guess it

    Read it from the Cloud console or from the CLI. Never hardcode it.

    bp cloud teams ls
  2. Invite the second account, as the owner

    The response carries an accept_url — you need it in step 3.

  3. Accept in a browser signed in as the SECOND account

    Open the accept_url while signed in as the invitee, not as the owner. This is the step that most often goes wrong silently — an owner-session accept produces a seat that looks right and tests nothing.

  4. Verify the role actually landed as member

    The new row must read role=member — not admin. If it reads admin, the RBAC leg is untested and the gate is not discharged.

  5. Log in as that member
    bp login       # complete the device-link flow as the SECOND account
  6. Re-run the smoke on the member's token

    Expect 13 ok. Keep the transcript — it is the evidence.

    tooling/mobile-smoke/smoke.sh

The two calls, exactly:

POST/v1/teams/:team_id/invitations
NameInTypeRequired
team_idpathuuidYes
emailbodystringYes
GET/v1/teams/:team_id/members
NameInTypeRequired
team_idpathuuidYes
The failure that matters If the smoke passes as the owner but fails as the member, that is precisely the bug this gate was built to catch. Stop and report it — do not retry with an admin token, which would turn a real finding into a green tick.

Gate 2 — APNs and FCM credentials

The relay is built right up to the credential wall. Six values go into /opt/barkpark-cloud/.env on the control plane. The two platforms are independent — Android alone is a valid, useful state, so do not block on Apple if you only have Google.

If you are waiting on Apple verification Do the Google half FIRST — it needs no Apple involvement at all. The platforms are independent and Android alone is a valid state, so while an Apple enrolment sits in verification you can complete FCM end to end: enable FCM API V1, take the service-account JSON, land it in the .env, restart, and register the relay. That satisfies criterion 1 (credential_status true for at least one platform) AND criterion 2 (the workspace-scoped webhook row) — this gate reaches 2 of 3 with zero Apple. Nothing is redone when APNs arrives; the two platforms sit side by side in the same .env.
You need your OWN Apple team. Being a member of other orgs does not give you one.

There is no "create an organization" button in the portal. Teams are not created — they are the RESULT of enrolling. Invitations add your Apple ID to other people's teams; they never produce a team of your own. Your existing Apple ID can hold your own membership alongside every membership you already have.

Choose Individual / Sole Proprietor, not Organization. Both cost $99/year and both grant the identical technical capability — App IDs, APNs keys, the push entitlement. Organization only adds a company name and member roles, and it demands a D-U-N-S number (days to obtain), a public functional website on your own domain, a legal entity, and authority to bind it. Individual needs none of that.

RequirementIndividual / Sole ProprietorOrganization
D-U-N-S numberNoRequired
Public website on own domainNoRequired
Legal entity + binding authorityNoRequired
Two-factor on the Apple AccountRequiredRequired
Legal name, no nicknamesRequiredRequired
Physical address (P.O. box rejected)RequiredRequired
Annual cost$99$99

Enrol at developer.apple.com/programs/enroll on the web, or through the Apple Developer app on an iPhone or iPad — the app route is usually smoother because it verifies your identity using the device. Fee waivers exist for nonprofits, accredited schools and government entities.

The trap once you have several teams: APNs keys and App IDs belong to ONE specific team. The App ID for cloud.barkpark.mobile and the APNs key must live in the SAME team — yours. A key from one team paired with an App ID from another fails authentication in a way that looks like a bad device token, which sends you hunting the wrong bug. Check the team selector on the account page before creating either one.

If you would rather not pay: should you hold Account Holder or Admin role in an org you are already a member of, you could create the App ID and key there instead — but that ties this app's identity to someone else's organization. Not recommended for your own product.

Where each value comes from: the APNs key, key id and team id from Apple's Keys page (create a key with the Apple Push Notifications service enabled — token-based APNs docs); the bundle id must already exist with the Push capability on Apple's Identifiers page; the FCM service-account JSON from Firebase → Service accounts, with FCM API V1 enabled.

Env varWhat it isThe trap that makes it silently useless
APNS_KEY_P8Full .p8 PEM contentsA single-line value with literal \n works — runtime.exs expands it
APNS_KEY_ID10-character key id—
APNS_TEAM_ID10-character team id—
APNS_BUNDLE_IDcloud.barkpark.mobileMUST equal ios.bundleIdentifier in apps/mobile/app.json, and that App ID must have Push registered
APNS_ENVsandbox or productionWrong value = every send 400s with BadDeviceToken
FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSONThe whole service-account file, verbatimFCM API V1 must be enabled on the project
  1. Write the six values and restart
    sudo vi /opt/barkpark-cloud/.env      # add the six values
# then restart the control plane
  2. Probe the credential status

    It must report true for at least one platform before you go further.

    # in a remote console:
BarkparkCloud.Push.credential_status()
  3. Register the relay once — it is idempotent, team-admin
  4. Verify the webhook row is WORKSPACE-SCOPED

    The created chat_blocked row must have a non-nil workspace_id. A flat-path row gets nil and can never fire — it looks installed and is inert.

POST/v1/barkparks/b2b81e69-c79c-4eff-b6d7-84507d15b925/push-relay
NameInTypeRequired
idpathuuid (guerrilla)Yes
The ceiling, stated plainly Not in this packet by construction: the client half — expo-notifications, the aps-environment entitlement, google-services.json. That needs the entitlements wave and a paid Apple membership. This is why Gate 3 can never retire Gate 2. Without a paid membership, do the server half above and record "client half parked — no paid Apple membership" as the blocker. That is a clean outcome, not a failure.

Gate 3 — device boot

Honest sizing: not minutes. The OS upgrade comes first — roughly 2 to 4 hours, almost all unattended download. Expo Go cannot work here, because MMKV v4 and react-native-nitro-modules are custom native modules; a dev build is mandatory.

Part A — toolchain only. No Apple account needed, and it discharges every layout clause on the Simulator.

  1. Install macOS Tahoe 26.5.2

    About 9.4 GiB, one restart. Do not stop at Sequoia 15.7.7 — it reaches only Xcode 26.0–26.3, below Expo SDK 56's floor of 26.4.

    softwareupdate --list-full-installers   # then install Tahoe 26.5.2
  2. Install Xcode 26.4 or newer

    Xcode on the App Store (~10–17 GiB). Launch it once so it installs components, then point Command Line Tools at Xcode — today they are CLT 16.4.

    sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer
xcodebuild -version
  3. Install CocoaPods via Homebrew — not gem

    System Ruby is 2.6.10, below CocoaPods' 2.7.4 floor. Homebrew ships its own Ruby.

    brew install cocoapods
  4. Prebuild the iOS project

    No ios/ directory is committed — this project is managed / CNG prebuild.

    pnpm install
cd apps/mobile
npx expo prebuild -p ios
  5. Boot it on the Simulator

    Needs no Apple ID. This covers the Class-B reflow sites, token geometry, the recycleItems decision, the archived shelf, the picker sheet, and blocks-in-chat with Mermaid islands.

    npx expo run:ios

Part B — physical iPhone, on a free Personal Team. Only if you actually have one. No iPhone has ever been paired to this Mac, so this is a question, not an assumption.

  1. Prepare the device

    Enable Developer Mode (the device restarts), then trust this Mac over USB.

  2. Sign with a free Apple ID

    Xcode → Settings → Accounts → add your Apple ID → automatic signing. The bundle id cloud.barkpark.mobile works as-is.

  3. Run on hardware
    npx expo run:ios --device
  4. Capture everything in ONE sitting

    Free Personal Team profiles expire after 7 days. Record: haptics feel across the registry including the needsYou warning; transcript scroll and fps plus follow mode; swipe-to-archive; and cascade auto-select with MRU across a relaunch.

    Before any MRU evidence counts, assert that MMKV is the live backing store and not the silent in-memory fallback — otherwise the MRU proof is vacuous.

If there is no iPhone — what to do instead

Record "no iPhone exists" as an explicit ruling on the task. The Simulator dispositions from Part A then become the discharge surface — the task's own criterion allows exactly this — and I will re-scope the affected root criteria.
